article.dek: The evening board re-dealt all three cards to Sunday's Bears-Jets game, Thursday's inactives are final, and Justin Jefferson missed practice again.

items.headline: The evening board put all three cards on Bears-Jets
paragraphs: The evening board re-dealt the whole table. All three cards now point at Sunday's Jets-Bears game in Chicago (1:00 p.m. ET kickoff). The app expects the Bears to win by about five and a half.

Hit Rate — the most-likely-to-win pick, not the +EV one — reads Bears moneyline at -175 on DraftKings. The app gives Chicago a 70.1% chance to win outright. Remember the app's own line: Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate.

Balanced and Value both read Bears -3.5 at -102 on FanDuel: a 50.5% cover chance for +3.2% expected value, MEDIUM reliability. The app's fair price is -105 — FanDuel is dealing three cents better than fair.

The app still projects Case Keenum as Chicago's starter and Geno Smith for the Jets. Ben Johnson has not named a Week 4 starter. If he names one after the board, the board is behind — run your book's line through Check.
items.takeaway: One game, three different questions: most likely to win, the middle ground, the +EV read.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: Thursday night is final. Pittsburgh's Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and Brandin Echols (concussion) are both ACTIVE after being questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle (toe) is OUT, so Jaylen Warren gets the workhorse role again — 17 carries for 127 yards last week. One correction from this morning: Joey Porter Jr. wasn't ruled out; he was traded to Dallas for a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder.

Cleveland is thin up front: center Elgton Jenkins (concussion), guard Teven Jenkins (back), and receiver Tylan Wallace (knee) are all OUT. Luke Wypler starts at center. The game kicked off at 8:15 p.m. ET — it's underway now.

Sunday's watch list starts with Justin Jefferson. The Vikings' star receiver missed practice again Thursday — two straight days with the ankle sprain. He's day-to-day, the scans showed nothing long-term, and Kevin O'Connell says they won't rush him. Friday's practice is the tell. Dolphins at Vikings, Sunday.

Elsewhere: Puka Nacua (Rams) got limited work in and is expected to play Sunday. Nico Collins (Texans) practiced Wednesday and is on track. Mike Evans (49ers) sat out again with a stack of injuries — no clarity until Friday.
items.takeaway: Thursday's question marks are answered. Sunday's start with Jefferson's ankle.

items.headline: Weather: dry tonight, Sunday's forecasts land tomorrow
paragraphs: Tonight's game is being played under the forecast from this morning: around 77 degrees at kickoff, cloudy, wind near 9 mph, rain chance in the single digits. Nothing that changes football.
Sunday's outdoor games get their final kickoff-window forecasts tomorrow. There are no Friday games.
items.takeaway: No weather worry tonight; Sunday's weather check lands in tomorrow's editions.

items.headline: When the price disappears, the card moves
paragraphs: This morning's Balanced card read Patriots +6.5 at even money on DraftKings. That price is gone. DraftKings now deals Bills -7 at -105, and FanDuel holds -6.5 but charges -122. So the card moved — to Bears -3.5 at -102.
Same story on Hit Rate: Bills moneyline went from -290 to -305 on DraftKings (-340 on FanDuel), and the card re-dealt to Bears moneyline -175 instead.

The cards read prices, not teams. When the number the card needed disappears, the card goes looking for a new one. That's not the app changing its mind about the Bills — it's the market moving the price tag.
And it cuts both ways: if YOUR book still shows Patriots +6.5 at even money, the morning read may still apply to your number. Don't guess — tap Check and type in what you can actually bet.
items.takeaway: The card follows the price. Your book's price is the one that matters.

items.headline: The Bears still haven't named a quarterback — that's what Check is for
paragraphs: Ben Johnson stayed non-committal Monday and Tuesday, and nothing changed today. The app projects Case Keenum — that's the app's read, not an announcement. (Keenum's Monday night: 24 of 34, 247 yards, two passing touchdowns and one on the ground, 27-7 over the Eagles.)
The board refreshes every morning and evening. News doesn't wait for the board. If Johnson names Bagent on Friday, the evening board won't know — and neither will the cards.

That's when you tap Check: type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through NFL EDGE's model and the evaluator and returns a bet-or-no-bet verdict on YOUR price. A full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Board stale, or your book's number isn't the board's? Check, don't guess.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Bills and Patriots prices moved; the board caught all of it
paragraphs: Patriots-Bills: the +6.5 at even money on DraftKings is gone — it's Bills -7 at -105 now. FanDuel still shows -6.5 but juiced to -122. Price mechanics: at -122, every $1.22 you risk wins $1 — you're paying extra for the same 6.5 points. Bills moneyline: -290 to -305 on DraftKings, -340 on FanDuel.
Bears -3.5: FanDuel still -102, DraftKings -105. That's the number both the Balanced and Value cards are reading.
Tonight's game held all day: Browns +2.5 at even money on both books, total 37.5 to 38.5. It's underway now, so those prices are history.
The evening board is priced off all of these numbers. If your book shows something different on any of them, the board's read doesn't apply to your number — run it through Check.
items.takeaway: The moves are in the board. Bet your book's number, not the board's.

items.headline: Sunday prep: Friday tells you who's actually playing
paragraphs: Final injury designations land Friday. The single biggest tell left this week: whether Justin Jefferson practices. If he's a full go Friday, the worry fades; if he sits again, plan as if he's out.
Then Sunday, inactive lists land about 90 minutes before each kickoff. That's when the last game-time decisions get made — like Ramsey and Echols tonight.
items.takeaway: Check back tomorrow evening — the injury picture sharpens on Friday.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: steam move
paragraphs: A steam move is a sudden line shift when a wave of respected money hits one side at several books in a short window. Example: the Bills went from -6.5 to -7 at DraftKings this afternoon. That's the market re-pricing, not one book guessing.
A steam move is a price alert, not a pick. It tells you where the money went — not who's right. And sometimes, like tonight, it just moves the card off a price that no longer exists.
items.takeaway: Steam = the price moved fast. It doesn't tell you which side to take.
